newsitem.title: USA: Miami expects budget shortfall for fiscal 1997.
newsitem.headline: Miami expects budget shortfall for fiscal 1997.

text.p: Miami expects a budget shortfall for fiscal 1997, but the size of the deficit will not be made public until city officials outline proposed remedies at a budget meeting on Thursday.

Mayor Joe Carollo has said the shortfall is at least $25 million, or about 10 percent of the $250 million operating budget. Acting City Merrett Stierheim did not return Reuter calls over several days, but has already apprised rating analysts of the problem.

"What he told me specifically is they were identifying the size of the shortfall, there was a shortfall," said John Incorvaia, a vice president at Moody's Investors Service. "They're trying to identify the magnitude of the problem and they want to present that along with the remedies at the Thursday meeting."
Incorvaia said Stierheim assured him the city would be able to make debt service payments on all of its bonds.
"They are not affected and they are fully budgeted for," he quoted Stierheim as saying.
Moody's cut Miami's general obligation bond rating from A1 to single-A in 1992. Incorvaia said it was too early to tell whether the budget problem would have any credit impact.
"We're talking about a budget imbalance going into fiscal 1997, which they are on the front end of and they can make some response to it," he said.
The city begins fiscal 1997 on Oct 1.
An official at Standard & Poor's Corp, which also rates Miami's GO debt single-A, said it was aware of the shortfall although the analyst involved was not available for comment Wednesday.

City Manager Cesar resgined on Sept 12 after he was charged by federal prosecutors with bribery conspiracy in connection with city contracts. He had been scheduled to submit his budget to city commissioners that same day, and said at the time that the proposed budget was balanced.
Incorvaia said he asked Stierheim whether the problems were on the revenue or expenditure side and "He suggested it was going to be a little of both."
Last year the city was forced to eliminate 428 positions thorugh layoffs and early retirements in order to balance its budget.
The city is near the state's 10-mill limit on property taxes for operating costs, and any effort to raise taxes or fees would be politically difficult in light of the corruption charges.
City Commissioner Miller Dawkins was also charged in the bribery case, and prosecutors said former City Finance Director Manohar Surana had agreed to plead guilty on related charges.
Surana resigned in August, shortly before federal prosecutors revealed he had worn a hidden wire to record conversations implicating Odio, Dawkins and a well-known lobbyist.
